items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, computational biology, bioinformatics, biology, engineering, statistics, mathematics, biology, or a related field.
At least 5 years of directly relevant experience in cancer research, including software engineering, scientific computing, bioinformatics, or computational modeling.
Deep functional experience leveraging advanced artificial intelligence modalities, expansive language architectures, and advanced latent-variable extraction techniques to cancer or biomedical data.
Experience with multi-omic datasets and cutting-edge translational research workflows, including the computational analysis of complex disease models and deeply stratified patient cohorts.

The Bioinformatics Programmer will develop, validate, and maintain predictive machine learning workflows for cancer research. The successful candidate will architect advanced, high-throughput computational frameworks focusing on structural informatics, foundational deep learning architectures, advanced latent variable extraction, and integrative analyses across highly complex multi-omic, molecular, and clinical datasets, with emphasis on reproducible research, translational impact, and high-quality software development. This role is intended for an experienced technical specialist who can contribute at a senior level through demonstrated productivity, independent execution, and strong analytical judgment.
40% - AI, Machine Learning & Computational Modeling
40% - Multi-Omics Analytics, Data Engineering & Reproducible Workflows
15% - Translational Research & Scientific Collaboration
5% - Technical Leadership, Mentorship & Methodological Innovation
Understanding of relational databases, web interfaces, and operating systems.
Familiarity with survival analysis, classification, clustering, and model interpretation
Demonstrated productivity through peer-reviewed publications, preprints, open-source software, internal tools, technical reports, or comparable documented work.
Familiarity with workflow managers, containerization, and high-performance computing.
Strong proficiency in Python and/or R.
Evidence of technical leadership or mentorship in collaborative research settings.
Demonstrated, long-term functional expertise in predictive modeling, advanced statistical modeling, the extraction of complex latent biological features, and high-dimensional data analysis.
Proven capacity to engineer distributed computational pipelines and deploy highly optimized multi-omic algorithms for large-scale data ingestion and analysis.
Thorough knowledge of bioinformatics methods, applications programming, web development and data structures.

Demonstrated capability in computational structural biology, specifically encompassing the advanced simulation of macromolecular interactions, dynamic conformational analysis, and complex drug-target elucidations
Thorough knowledge of bioinformatics programming design, modification and implementation.
Strong project management skills.
Thorough knowledge of modern biology and applicable field of research.
Communication skills to work with both technical and non-technical personnel in multiple fields of expertise and at various levels in the organization.
Ability to communicate technical information in a clear and concise manner.
Ability to interface with management on a regular basis.
Self motivated, work independently or as part of a team, able to learn quickly, meet deadlines and demonstrate problem solving skills.
Thorough knowledge of web, application and data security concepts and methods.
Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities, and deliver reliable results.
